# FAQ

#### Is frozen-duckdb really a drop-in replacement for duckdb-rs?

Yes — same API, same functionality, no code changes needed; builds are 99% faster.

#### What does "Failed to get frozen DuckDB binary" mean?

The builder could not obtain the DuckDB library at all: no cached binary,
the release-asset download failed, and the local source-compile fallback
also failed. The panic comes from the sys-crate build script; read the
error tail for the underlying cause. A normal first-time local compile
logs its progress and only uses this panic when it fails.

#### What if no cached binary is found?

The builder downloads the matching per-arch release asset, or compiles the bundled DuckDB 2.0.0-dev source locally when the download fails (the supported Linux and pre-release
path). Check ~/.frozen-duckdb/cache/ afterwards; try cargo clean followed by a
rebuild if the state looks stale.

#### What does the ARCH environment variable do?

The builder detects the architecture in order: explicit single-slice
CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES → ARCH → uname -m (multi-arch lists and unknown values
fall through to host detection). An explicit single-slice value drives the
builder's detection, cache placement, and asset naming — not just
prebuilt/setup_env.sh and the architecture helper module
(`frozen_duckdb::architecture::detect()`).

#### Which platforms are supported?

macOS uses prebuilt per-arch dylibs (arm64 and x86_64). Linux uses
prebuilt `.so` files and needs glibc 2.38 or newer. Windows compiles the
pinned DuckDB 2.0.0-dev source locally. The crate version is 2.0.0.

#### Why is it called frozen?

The DuckDB mega-library is compiled once, then frozen into prebuilt binaries downloaded from GitHub Releases and cached under ~/.frozen-duckdb/ — builds take seconds instead of minutes.
